function: RIS configuration: linear regression maps user-2 position to the hybrid-RIS partition (N1 active elements for U-1, N2 passive for U-2) in uplink NOMA; phases are analytic (pp. 4-5).
system: Hybrid RIS (active + passive parts), N=128-512; two users, single-antenna BS, uplink NOMA, quasi-static flat Rayleigh fading, 5 GHz, 20 m x 20 m outdoor (pp. 4, 7).
method: Supervised linear regression trained offline on a fingerprint database (U-2 position to optimal N1 found by an iterative search), RMSE loss; online inference of the partition (pp. 5-6).
data_channel: Own simulator: flat Rayleigh fading, 3GPP UMi path loss at 5 GHz, 10^4 realizations; labels from iterative algorithm [43] at 36 or 484 training positions (pp. 5, 7).
test_conditions: Trained on 36 or 484 U-2 positions; tested at (13,13), 0.8 m from a training point, and at (8,8), 2 m away, distant from trained points (p. 8).
baselines: Non-learned: iterative RIS-partition search of [43] (Jain-fairness objective); fully passive RIS NOMA and fully active RIS OMA (TDMA). No earlier learned method compared (pp. 5, 8-9).
metrics: Per-user achievable rates and ergodic sum rate (fairness), outage probability (theory and simulation), BER, elapsed run time (pp. 7-10).
complexity: Measured run time (Table II): trained model 0.314/0.660/2.013 s versus iterative algorithm 1.970/5.567/18.936 s for N=128/256/512, Pt=16 dBm (pp. 7-8).
q1_support: p. 7: "The path loss for 5 GHz is modeled using the 3GPP Urban Micro (UMi) technique as described in [46]." Only the path loss follows 3GPP (TR 36.814); the fading is the authors' own quasi-static flat Rayleigh model (p. 4); no TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 8: "performance at locations that are distant from the trained points" is Fig. 5(b), U-2 at (8,8), 2 m from a training point, in the same site with the same channel model and RIS size; I count it as a held-out position, not a new scenario (borderline).
q3_support: p. 7: "elapsed run time for the trained model is compared to that of an iterative algorithm [43]" The only comparators are the non-learned iterative search of [43] and fully passive NOMA or OMA schemes; no earlier learned partitioning method is compared, and the 36-TP and 484-TP models are variants of the proposed one.
q4_support: p. 8: "the trained model took only 0.659863 seconds, while the iterative algorithm took 5.567032 seconds" for 256 elements; Table II (p. 7) gives measured run times for 128, 256 and 512 elements.
q5_support: p. 5: "a fingerprint database is established, which contains recorded positional data at different reference points of U-2" The labels come from the authors' own iterative search on simulated channels; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included as area 3: the learned element is a linear regression that sets the hybrid-RIS partition (N1, N2), a RIS configuration; the RIS phases are analytic alignments (p. 4). Labels come from the authors' group's iterative algorithm [43]. q2 is borderline: Fig. 2 (p. 5) shows training points only outside the lower-left 10 m x 10 m square, and Fig. 5(b) tests U-2 at (8,8) inside it, but the site, channel model and RIS size are unchanged, so I counted a held-out position; the reviewer may prefer 1.
